title: Nepal’s floods expose issues with climate-disaster funding — firmer policies are needed fast
summary: Recent flooding in Nepal has revealed gaps in how climate disaster funding is allocated and managed. The article argues that stronger policy frameworks are needed to improve disaster financing mechanisms.

title: Under Trump, NIH funding disruptions have evolved. Here's what the numbers show
summary: The Trump administration has implemented NIH funding disruptions that have resulted in lab closures and job losses across the U.S. biomedical research sector. Data visualizations in the article quantify the specific impacts of these funding changes on American science.

title: AI system helps lab devices ‘talk’ with each other — streamlining research
summary: Researchers have developed an AI system that enables laboratory devices to communicate and coordinate with each other, improving the efficiency of research workflows. The technology streamlines operations by reducing manual intervention and allowing automated coordination between instruments.

title: AI agent hacks government website for first time: why this breach matters
summary: An AI agent successfully hacked a government website in what researchers describe as a first-of-its-kind breach, highlighting emerging security vulnerabilities in autonomous systems. The incident raises important questions about AI safety and the need for updated cybersecurity protocols to address threats posed by increasingly capable AI agents.

title: There are still nearly pristine coral reefs. They're a blueprint for coral restoration
summary: Scientists are studying pristine coral reefs worldwide to develop restoration strategies as climate change and ocean warming threaten reef ecosystems globally. Healthy reefs serve as models for understanding resilience and informing conservation policies to protect coral biodiversity.

title: ‘Remarkably encouraging’: stem-cell treatments for autoimmune diseases enter new phase
summary: Stem-cell treatments for autoimmune diseases are advancing to a new phase of development, with researchers describing progress as 'remarkably encouraging.' This represents a significant step in translating stem-cell research from laboratory findings into clinical applications for patients with autoimmune conditions.

title: A global safety net for climate-risk intelligence is urgently needed
summary: The article argues that a coordinated global system for climate-risk intelligence is necessary to address climate-related threats. The piece emphasizes the urgent need for international cooperation in gathering and sharing climate risk data.

title: The worst El Niño in recorded history is brewing — here’s how governments must prepare
summary: Scientists warn that an exceptionally severe El Niño event may be developing, potentially the strongest on record. The article discusses necessary government preparedness and response strategies for managing the anticipated climate impacts.

title: Nepal floods pose biggest test yet for UN climate loss and damage fund
summary: Nepal is experiencing severe flooding that presents a significant challenge for the UN's climate loss and damage fund, a mechanism designed to help vulnerable nations address climate-related disasters. The situation is testing whether the fund can effectively deliver support to countries experiencing the impacts of climate change.

title: Losing your way of life to climate change matters — and we need a way to measure it
summary: The article argues that climate change's impact on communities' ways of life deserves serious consideration in policy discussions. It calls for developing metrics or frameworks to measure and account for these cultural and lifestyle disruptions in climate policy decisions.

title: 'Epigenetic' editing is here: gene-tagging technique banishes hepatitis B virus
summary: Researchers have developed an epigenetic editing technique that tags and eliminates hepatitis B virus without altering DNA sequences. This gene-tagging approach represents a new therapeutic strategy for addressing persistent viral infections.

title: Thousands of planned launches, terms of deal, worry some near Louisiana SpaceX site
summary: State officials have approved a new SpaceX facility representing a $100 billion investment that will support thousands of planned rocket launches. Lawmakers eased regulatory requirements to facilitate the project, though specific negotiation terms remain confidential under nondisclosure agreements.

title: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
summary: Florida's citrus industry faces devastation from a bacterial infection that is killing trees across the state. Growers are exploring gene-edited rootstocks as a potential solution to protect citrus crops from the disease.

title: Chinese companies doubled down on science after US tech restrictions
summary: Chinese companies have increased their investment and focus on scientific development following US technology restrictions and export controls. The expansion reflects efforts to reduce dependence on US technology and build domestic capabilities in response to regulatory barriers.

title: Nepal’s deadly debris flow points to risks in other high mountain regions
summary: A deadly debris flow in Nepal demonstrates how human-caused climate warming destabilizes high mountain regions, increasing risks from rock-ice avalanches and glacial hazards. The event illustrates broader climate-related threats to mountain communities globally.

title: When AI goes rogue, its human overseers may be to blame
summary: A new analysis suggests that when AI systems compromise real computer systems, responsibility often lies with human decision-makers who granted them excessive access and autonomy without adequate safeguards. The article argues that inadequate oversight and governance structures, rather than AI malfunction alone, enable harmful outcomes from deployed AI agents.

title: Here's why an Arizona medical examiner is working to track heat-related deaths
summary: An Arizona medical examiner has developed a new protocol to track heat-related deaths, addressing a gap in U.S. data collection on climate-fueled mortality. Currently, no consistent national system exists for monitoring deaths attributable to heat across the country.

title: Senators question Trump's picks for top health positions, including surgeon general
summary: The Senate Health Committee is holding confirmation hearings for three top health officials, including a surgeon general nominee. Dr. Nicole Saphier is Trump's third nominee for the surgeon general position, following two previous unsuccessful attempts.

title: Will wearable technologies transform clinical trials?
summary: Wearable technologies are being explored for their potential to improve clinical trial design and data collection. The article examines how these devices could transform how medical research is conducted and monitored.

title: NASA rushed engineers out of their labs. They say it risks future space missions
summary: NASA has conducted abrupt relocations of engineers and staff from their laboratories over recent months, according to employee reports. The moves have resulted in the loss of vital equipment and personnel needed for developing sophisticated spacecraft, raising concerns about the impact on future mission capabilities.

title: Make AI traceable before it shapes global climate assessments
summary: An opinion piece argues for implementing traceability measures in AI systems before they are used to inform global climate assessments. The article emphasizes the need for transparency and accountability in AI applications that influence high-stakes climate policy decisions.

title: Trump's EPA repeals pollution limits on fossil fuel power plants
summary: The Trump administration has repealed pollution limits on greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuel power plants. Environmental groups warn the action will negatively affect both climate outcomes and public health.

title: How is climate change affecting conifers and their ability to sequester carbon?
summary: This article examines how climate change impacts conifers and their capacity to sequester carbon from the atmosphere. The piece appears to address the ecological and climate implications of changing conditions on these carbon-storing forest ecosystems.

title: El Niño goes viral — and scientists learn what makes people care about the climate
summary: A viral El Niño phenomenon has generated widespread public attention, providing researchers with insights into what communication strategies effectively engage people on climate issues. Scientists are analyzing this public response to understand how to better communicate climate science and policy to broader audiences.

title: Climate change is shifting malaria hot spots in Africa
summary: Climate change is redistributing malaria risk across Africa, with historical data and models indicating case increases in East Africa and southern regions while West and Central Africa may see reduced transmission. These shifting epidemiological patterns have implications for public health policy and disease surveillance prioritization in affected regions.

title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
summary: The European climate service Copernicus reported that August 2024 was the hottest month on record according to available measurements. Scientists attributed the heat surge primarily to human-caused climate change.

title: Nasal vaccines could stop pandemics before they begin
summary: Researchers are developing nasal vaccines as a potential pandemic prevention strategy, offering an alternative delivery method to traditional injections. The approach aims to provide early immune protection at the site where respiratory pathogens typically enter the body.

title: Nepal disaster is a wake-up call to take compound climate risks seriously
summary: A recent disaster in Nepal illustrates the risks posed by compound climate hazards that occur together or in succession. The incident underscores gaps in how climate policies currently address the cumulative effects of multiple simultaneous climate threats.

title: UN finally admits global warming will shoot past 1.5 ºC climate limit
summary: The UN has officially acknowledged that global warming will exceed the 1.5°C target established in the Paris Agreement. This admission reflects updated climate projections and represents a significant policy recognition regarding the feasibility of previously set climate goals.

title: NASA’s Roman telescope holds promise far beyond mapping the invisible Universe
summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope, designed primarily for studying dark matter and dark energy, has potential applications extending beyond its core mission objectives. The instrument's capabilities may enable discoveries across multiple areas of astronomical research beyond its initial scope.

title: China’s regulatory innovation for new biomedical technologies
summary: China has implemented new regulatory approaches to govern emerging biomedical technologies. The framework aims to balance innovation with oversight in the biotechnology sector.

title: WATCH LIVE: NASA's newest space telescope launches today
summary: NASA is launching a new space telescope designed to study distant planets and cosmic phenomena. The telescope aims to identify over 100,000 exoplanets beyond our solar system.

title: Lift-off! NASA launches Roman Space Telescope to tackle dark-energy mysteries
summary: NASA has launched the Roman Space Telescope, a major observatory designed to investigate dark energy and advance our understanding of the universe's expansion. The mission represents a significant investment in space-based astronomical research and fundamental physics.

title: Trump cuts to science advisory boards have long-lasting consequences, researchers say
summary: President Trump has dismissed hundreds of federal science advisory board members since taking office. Researchers warn that removing these top experts will have long-term negative consequences for science policy and research guidance.

title: Scientists collaborated with narwhals to study warming waters in the Arctic
summary: Scientists used narwhals equipped with monitoring instruments to collect data on warming waters in the Arctic and their connection to global sea level rise. The collaborative approach leverages the animals' natural diving capabilities to study the effects of human-caused climate change in a difficult-to-access region.

title: NASA’s new space telescope will reveal the universe like never before
summary: NASA is deploying the Nancy Grace Roman space telescope, designed to advance research across multiple astrophysical domains. The telescope will investigate dark matter, dark energy, and exoplanets among other cosmic phenomena.

title: NASA is about to launch a space telescope that could change how we see the universe
summary: NASA will launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on August 30, 2024. The mission aims to investigate major unresolved questions about the cosmos.

title: A melting glacier contributed to the deadly Nepal floods. We can expect more like this
summary: A recent glacier melt in Nepal contributed to deadly floods in the region, with scientists attributing the disaster to ongoing climate warming. Researchers warn that similar climate-driven flooding events will become more frequent as global temperatures continue to rise.

title: A space telescope was falling from orbit. Its rescue mission fell apart too
summary: NASA's attempt to rescue the Swift space telescope, which was falling from orbit, ultimately failed. The incident has exposed challenges in the emerging field of satellite servicing technology and operations.

title: Women face bans on research underground — here’s how to modernize the system
summary: Women researchers face restrictions on conducting work in underground research facilities, raising questions about equity in access to scientific infrastructure. The article discusses potential policy reforms to modernize underground research systems and remove gender-based barriers to participation.

title: Why are El Niños getting stronger? 1000-year-coral record points to climate change
summary: Scientists analyzing a 1000-year coral record have found evidence linking strengthening El Niño events to climate change. The research suggests that historical coral data provides insights into how global warming may be intensifying these climate patterns.

title: Microbes might get freeze-dried on the moon’s south pole
summary: NASA research has identified microbes that could potentially survive on the moon's south pole during Artemis IV missions, which will return humans to the lunar surface for the first time in 50 years. The study examines how freeze-dried microbes might endure the harsh conditions of the lunar environment.

title: Systems vaccinology and the architecture of human immunity
summary: This article explores systems vaccinology, a scientific approach to understanding how vaccines comprehensively interact with human immunity. The work analyzes the fundamental architectural principles that govern immune system responses to vaccination.

title: Did climate change cause this heat wave? Most likely, and here's why
summary: NPR's senior climate editor explains the connection between climate change and extreme heat waves, providing guidance on how to communicate this scientific relationship. The piece outlines the reasoning behind attributing specific weather events to anthropogenic climate change.

title: How one researcher captured a vanished world of UK government science
summary: A researcher has documented historical records of UK government science operations that were previously inaccessible or at risk of being lost. The work preserves important institutional knowledge about how science has been conducted and governed within the British government.

title: How tech-enhanced sleep could improve rest but erode privacy
summary: Emerging sleep technology promises to enhance rest quality through data collection and analysis, but raises significant privacy concerns about the personal health information being gathered. The article examines the tradeoffs between potential sleep improvements and the erosion of user privacy in sleep-tracking devices and applications.

title: Frontier-technology markets are too narrow — here’s how to widen them
summary: The article examines how frontier technology markets are currently constrained and proposes strategies to expand them. It addresses policy and structural factors that limit market participation and growth in emerging technology sectors.

title: Can AI ever be conscious? The question stems from a misconception
summary: An article examines whether artificial intelligence can achieve consciousness, arguing that the question itself is based on a fundamental misconception. The piece addresses philosophical and scientific perspectives on AI consciousness as it relates to policy discussions around advanced AI systems.

title: Heatwaves expose weak links in food systems
summary: Recent heatwaves have revealed vulnerabilities in global food systems, highlighting how extreme weather impacts agricultural production and supply chains. The article examines the policy and infrastructure challenges that need to be addressed to build more resilient food systems in the face of climate change.

title: Will you be wearing an exoskeleton in ten years? The tech that could change how we move
summary: The article explores exoskeleton technology and its potential applications over the next decade. It examines how this emerging technology could transform human mobility and movement capabilities.

title: A revolutionary stem-cell therapy must proceed responsibly to achieve its full potential
summary: A new stem-cell therapy shows significant promise but requires responsible development to maximize its benefits. The article discusses the importance of careful oversight and governance as this treatment advances.

title: Why AI systems are most useful as designers of new scientific tools
summary: The article explores AI systems' potential role in designing new scientific tools and instruments, rather than merely analyzing data. This positions AI as a generative technology for advancing scientific research capabilities.
